info.title: iFixit API
info.description:
Our API provides programmatic access to iFixit, enabling anyone to write innovative
applications and utilities on top of our rich repair database.

**What can I do with the API?**

Anything you want! The sky is the limit for awesome applications built using our database
of repair guides. We can't wait to see what you come up with.

Our API is provided under a non-commercial BY-NC-SA license. If you'd like to use it for
commercial purposes, reach out to our [API team](mailto:api@ifixit.com) for pricing.
Training Large Language Models on iFixit content is prohibited by our
[Terms of Service](https://www.ifixit.com/Info/Terms_of_Use).

The API provides access to our repair guides (step-by-step guides and namespace pages),
categories, users, teams, and our reputation badges.

If you build on our API, we will support you by maintaining future compatibility. Make sure
to version your API calls with `2.0`. When we introduce changes that may break existing apps,
we will increment the version number.

## Using the API

### Getting Started

The best way to get started is to just dive right in! You don't need an app ID for most
requests, so you can start writing your app right now. Here's an example API call:

```
curl https://www.ifixit.com/api/2.0/guides/1220
```

If you want to build an offline tool, an archived collection of oManual files is also available.

### Authentication

Most public endpoints do not require authentication. A few endpoints require an App ID,
which you can request from our [API team](mailto:api@ifixit.com). This is usually only required for complex integrations.

To authenticate, first obtain a token with your email and password:

```
curl -X POST https://www.ifixit.com/api/2.0/user/token \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"email":"you@example.com","password":"yourpassword"}'
```

The response includes an `authToken` field. Use it in subsequent requests:

```
curl https://www.ifixit.com/api/2.0/user \
  -H "Authorization: api YOUR_AUTH_TOKEN"
```

Note: the `Authorization` header uses the `api` scheme, not `Bearer`.

### Response Format

All endpoints return JSON by default. Append `?pretty` to any request URL for
human-readable formatted output. Some endpoints additionally support XML via the
`Accept: application/xml` request header.

### Error Responses

Errors are returned as a JSON object with a consistent shape:

```json
{
  "error": true,
  "message": "Human-readable description of the error"
}
```

Common status codes:

| Code | Meaning |
|------|---------|
| 400 | Bad request — invalid parameters |
| 401 | Authentication required |
| 403 | Forbidden — insufficient privileges |
| 404 | Resource not found |
| 429 | Rate limit exceeded |

### Pagination

List endpoints accept `offset` and `limit` query parameters. `limit` defaults to 20
and has a maximum of 200. Responses are plain arrays — iterate by incrementing `offset`
by `limit` until you receive fewer items than requested.

```
GET /api/2.0/guides?offset=0&limit=50
GET /api/2.0/guides?offset=50&limit=50
```

### Rate Limiting

API requests are rate limited. When limits are exceeded, the API returns a `429` status code.

### Versioning

This is version 2.0 of the iFixit API. The version is included in the URL path: `/api/2.0/`.

The request body is the raw image file; the `file` query parameter supplies the filename, whose extension determines the file type (JPEG, GIF, PNG, BMP, TIFF, HEIC, WEBP, AVIF). post.description: Queues a job that creates a rotated copy of an existing image and swaps it into the authenticated user's media manager in place of the original (the original's library attachment is removed only when it belongs to the same user, and only after the copy is fully processed). The copy is a new source image, so later crops and markers apply to the rotated pixels. The `image` path segment accepts either an integer image id or a GUID string. The response is a job handle; clients poll `/user/media/images/rotate/{jobID}` until it reports `complete` or `failed`.

get.description: Reports the state of a rotation job queued by `rotateImageInMediaManager`. While the worker runs, `status` is `processing`. On success it is `complete` and `item` carries the new copy's flat media data; the worker generates display sizes before reporting success, so no further readiness polling is needed. `failed` means the original image and its library attachment are unchanged. Jobs are only visible to the user who queued them; unknown or another user's job ids return 404.

item.description: A single entry in a user's Media Manager library. The shape is flat and varies by media class (`type`): images carry `imageid`, documents carry `documentid`, and videos and embeds carry `objectid`. Size URL fields (`mini`, `thumbnail`, `standard`, `medium`, `original`) are present only for the sizes that have been generated at response time. When the request supplies an `accepts` filter collection, each item also carries a `filter_state`.

imageid.description: Image id for images; thumbnail image id for documents and embeds; `null` when there is no associated image

srcid.description: Source media id when this item is a derivative

filename.description: Original filename, or embed title for embeds

date.description: Upload or creation time as a UNIX timestamp

filter_state.description: Server-computed acceptability of a media item for the requested `accepts` filter collection. Clients branch on this value rather than re-deriving the rules: `true` when the item is attachable as-is, `"crop"` when it must be cropped before it can be attached, `false` when the item's type is not accepted, or an object carrying a `message` that explains a soft failure (for example, an image below the collection's minimum resolution).

get.description: Returns the guide's normal tags as a flat array of strings sorted alphabetically. A guide that is private, deleted, or nonexistent returns 403 with the message "Guide is private."; the endpoint does not return 404.

403.description: Guide is private, deleted, or does not exist. The body is `{"message": "Guide is private."}`.

put.description: Adds a normal tag to a guide, creating the tag if needed. Requires guide moderator privilege. The tag must be at most 32 characters. Tag text is mapped through the site's tag synonyms before storage, so the stored tag can differ from the submitted text. A prefix matching a tag type (for example `device:`) is parsed as a typed tag rather than literal text. Tag changes do not create a guide revision, so no `revisionid` parameter is required.

200.description: The updated guide. The guide object does not include a tags field; current tags are available from `getGuideTags`.

(CATEGORY namespace only). Each task can have multiple
triggers for "whichever comes first" logic.

items.description:
Defines when a maintenance task is due. When a schedule has multiple
triggers, the task is due when whichever trigger fires first.

trigger_type.description:
Type of trigger:
- `usage`: based on device usage (miles, hours, cycles, pages)
- `time`: based on elapsed calendar time
- `condition`: based on a metric crossing a threshold

metric.description:
What is being measured:
- For `usage` triggers: typically `usage` (matches the event `usage`/`usage_unit` fields)
- For `time` triggers: `elapsed_time`
- For `condition` triggers: the specific metric, e.g. `oil_life_percent`, `tire_tread_mm`

unit.description: Unit of measurement (miles, km, hours, pages, months, years, %, mm)

first_interval.description:
Interval for the first occurrence when it differs from
`repeat_interval` (for example, a timing belt first due at 90,000
miles). `null` means `repeat_interval` applies from the start.

repeat_interval.description:
Interval for subsequent occurrences (for example, an oil change
every 5,000 miles). Required for `usage` and `time` triggers.

threshold.description: Value the metric is compared against for `condition` triggers

items.description:
A maintenance or service event. Materialized events have a
`workbench_eventid` and are stored in the database; synthetic events
have `workbench_eventid: null` and are computed on the fly from
active maintenance schedules to represent the next upcoming
occurrence of a scheduled task. Synthetic events come from item-level
schedules (`workbench_item_maintenance_scheduleid`) or schedules
inherited from the item's device wiki
(`wiki_maintenance_scheduleid`); inherited schedules remain virtual
until the user completes, skips, or updates them, at which point an
item-level copy is created.

workbench_eventid.description: `null` for synthetic (computed) events; present for materialized (user-created) events.

date_event.description: UNIX timestamp of when the event occurred, is scheduled, or is next due. `null` for usage-only synthetic events.

usage.description: Absolute usage reading at time of event (e.g. odometer at 75000, battery at 312 cycles). Not a delta.

usage_unit.description: Unit for usage reading (e.g. miles, km, hours, cycles, pages)

cost.description: Cost of the maintenance event. `null` when not recorded and on synthetic events.

date_completed.description: UNIX timestamp of when the event was completed

date_skipped.description: UNIX timestamp of when the event was skipped. Mutually exclusive with `date_completed`.

date_created.description: UNIX timestamp when the event was created. `null` for synthetic events.

wiki_maintenance_scheduleid.description: Present on synthetic events from inherited wiki schedules that have not yet been materialized to the item; the wiki-schedule event operations address the event by this id. `null` once the schedule has been materialized, at which point `workbench_item_maintenance_scheduleid` is set instead.

items.description:
Defines when a maintenance task is due. Multiple triggers per schedule
implement "whichever comes first" logic.

trigger_type.description:
Type of trigger:
- `usage`: based on device usage (miles, hours, cycles, pages)
- `time`: based on elapsed calendar time
- `condition`: based on a metric crossing a threshold

metric.description:
What is being measured. Validated against a fixed allowlist per
trigger type:
- `usage` triggers: must be `usage`
- `time` triggers: must be `elapsed_time`
- `condition` triggers: one of `battery_cycle_count`,
  `battery_health_percent`, `belt_wear`, `brake_pad_thickness_mm`,
  `controller_runtime_hours`, `coolant_ph`, `filter_life_percent`,
  `filter_pressure_drop`, `oil_life`, `oil_life_percent`,
  `temperature_celsius`, `tire_tread_depth_mm`, `visible_wear`,
  `water_hardness`

unit.description: Unit of measurement, validated against a fixed allowlist per trigger type: `usage` accepts `miles`, `kilometers`, `hours`, `pages`, `cycles`; `time` accepts `days`, `weeks`, `months`, `years`; `condition` accepts `%`, `percent`, `score`, `hours`, `miles`, `kilometers`, `mm`, `psi`, `volts`, `celsius`, `fahrenheit`, `ph`, `count`. `km` is rejected — the accepted spelling is `kilometers`.

first_due_at.description: **Time triggers only.** Absolute UNIX timestamp of the first occurrence, for "first on date X, then repeat every N units." Ignored once the first occurrence has been completed or skipped; always `null` for usage and condition triggers. Treated as a UTC calendar date — send UTC midnight of the intended day.

first_interval.description: **Usage triggers only.** Usage threshold for the first occurrence, for "first at N units, then repeat every M units," expressed in the trigger's `unit`. Always `null` for time and condition triggers.

repeat_interval.description: Interval for subsequent occurrences. Required for usage/time triggers unless a first-occurrence anchor is given (`first_due_at` for time, `first_interval` for usage), and must be greater than zero. Must be a whole number for `months`/`years` units; use a finer unit for sub-month cadence.

threshold.description: Value to compare against for condition triggers

triggers.description: Current triggers of the event's schedule, reflecting live schedule state rather than a snapshot at event creation. `null` means the event has no schedule (one-off/manual event); `[]` means the schedule has no active triggers.
